title: French Bulldog Too Skinny? Why Your Frenchie Won't Gain Weight
description: Is your French Bulldog too skinny? How to check body condition, ideal Frenchie weight, why puppies fail to gain, and how to help your dog gain weight safely.

faq.q: How do I know if my French Bulldog is too skinny?
faq.a: If the ribs, spine and hip bones are visible from a distance and there is little muscle, your dog is too thin. At ideal weight you can feel the ribs easily under a thin layer of fat and see a waist from above.

faq.q: Why is my French Bulldog so skinny even though he eats?
faq.a: Unexplained weight loss despite appetite has several possible causes, including inadequate calories, parasites, malabsorption and other illness. Veterinary history, examination and selected tests help distinguish them.

faq.q: How can I make my French Bulldog gain weight?
faq.a: Rule out medical causes with your vet first. Then increase a complete, balanced food gradually, split into several meals, and weigh your dog weekly. Avoid table scraps.

faq.q: How much should a French Bulldog weigh?
faq.a: The AKC standard says no more than 28 lb, and the FCI standard gives about 18 to 31 lb depending on sex. Body condition matters more than an exact number.

faq.q: Why is my French Bulldog puppy not gaining weight?
faq.a: Growth rates differ by age and expected mature size. Use a veterinary puppy growth chart and contact a veterinarian promptly if the puppy loses weight, fails to gain or seems unwell.
